title: Proxy features and fairness
goals: Explain why removing one field does not guarantee fairness
Propose a contextual review with concrete evidence

prerequisite.prompt: Does equal overall accuracy prove fair treatment?
prerequisite.answer: No; examine errors, consequences, data and context.

vocabulary: A variable that can stand in for another characteristic
An observed association, not proof of cause
A characteristic requiring particular care in a context
A comparison that removes a feature or component

blocks.text: An input can carry information about a characteristic without naming it. In a fictional school-device dataset, device code may be associated with building or access to newer equipment. Removing a building field does not remove all related information. Do not infer a real student identity or protected characteristic in this exercise.

Use fictional classroom data throughout this investigation. Keep the task, units, reference labels and data split visible as you reason. Earlier weeks supplied the model-building process; this week examines proxy features and fairness.

Fictional records show device code X on 8 of 10 north-building examples and 2 of 10 south-building examples. Device and building are associated in this sample. This does not prove device causes model errors or that every X device comes from north. The remaining cases contradict such a universal rule.

Before continuing, underline the decision rule and circle the evidence that supports the conclusion. Explain the example to a partner without replacing the counts or conditions with a stronger claim. Keep the distinction between an observed result and a proposed next step.

blocks.title: Proxy features and fairness at a glance
blocks.caption: A feature may be legitimate for one purpose and inappropriate for another. Ask what is measured, when it is available, why it predicts and who might be disadvantaged. A correlation alone neither authorizes use nor proves harm. Talk through the intended decision and available alternatives.

blocks.label: Why might removing building but keeping device code leave related information? Explain the steps or evidence behind your response.

blocks.text: Compare versions with and without device code on the same validation cases, while checking subgroup errors and useful task performance. This ablation measures a change in that experiment; correlated inputs may still carry similar information. Retain group definitions and denominators, and avoid using the final test for repeated feature decisions.

Do not advertise fairness through unawareness merely because names or a sensitive field were removed. A classroom audit should state unresolved questions, intended non-use and a human review path. Never collect sensitive student information simply to fill this exercise.

blocks.label: Does unchanged accuracy after removing a proxy prove fairness?

workbook.title: Read an association
workbook.prompt: What do the device counts support, and what do they not support?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: X occurs 8/10 north and 2/10 south in this sample. This supports an association, not a deterministic identity rule or a causal explanation.

workbook.title: Find a proxy risk
workbook.prompt: Why might removing building but keeping device code leave related information?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Device code is associated with building in the sample and may carry some of that information indirectly.

workbook.title: Plan an ablation
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Use the same validation rows and metric, fit both versions only on training, and report overall and relevant subgroup errors with denominators.

workbook.title: Apply independently
workbook.prompt: A team removes postcode but retains school code and claims all location-related information is gone. Evaluate the claim and request evidence.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: The claim is unsupported: school code may be associated with location. Review provenance and associations, compare ablations and group errors, and state unresolved proxy risks.

workbook.title: Limit the result
workbook.prompt: Does unchanged accuracy after removing a proxy prove fairness?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: No. Other features can retain information and accuracy can hide different errors and consequences.

teacher.background: Teach two 45-minute sessions. This week focuses on proxy features and fairness. Model the worked example first, collect the new W 4 case independently before feedback, and use the fresh retry to check transfer. Award credit for traceable reasoning and bounded claims, including justified uncertainty.
materials: Paper, pencils and a calculator for fractions
The fictional examples and a blank evidence table
Saved classroom project records for critique; no personal student dataset required
sessions: Use the prerequisite question: Does equal overall accuracy prove fair treatment? Check the explanation before proceeding.
Read the opening and model the worked evidence. Ask students to identify proxy feature in context.
Complete W 1 and W 2 with support: read an association; find a proxy risk. Require the evidence, not only the final response.
Read the visual row by row. Collect the guided explanation and compare reasoning in pairs. Connect each conclusion to the stated evidence.
Retrieve the distinction between proxy feature and correlation. Invite a counterexample to an overconfident claim.
Discuss the application and complete W 3: Describe a controlled with/without-code comparison.
Collect W4 independently before giving hints. Assess these outcomes: Identify possible proxy features; Explain why removing one field does not guarantee fairness. Record any support used.
Use W 5 and the exit response to assess limits. Give targeted feedback, then the fresh retry. Save evidence of independent understanding.

teacher.assessment: For independent W 4, require: The claim is unsupported: school code may be associated with location. Review provenance and associations, compare ablations and group errors, and state unresolved proxy risks. Fresh retry: removing a device-brand field while retaining model number may leave brand-related information. Require a contextual association check and no automatic fairness claim. Mark each criterion as independent, supported or not yet demonstrated. Reassess the reasoning after feedback; do not replace the first attempt silently.
teacher.support: Provide a blank evidence table and allow a verbal explanation before writing. Highlight the given conditions without supplying the W 4 conclusion. Use proxy feature and correlation in full sentences. Extension: alter one condition in the worked example and explain which conclusion changes and which remains supported.
